reason: Attack failed on the wording, and it came close to succeeding. The verifier's evidence was two blog transcriptions, which is exactly the kind of agreement that proves nothing, and I found a rival reading almost at once: Wikiquote prints For nothing is fixed, forever and forever, it is not fixed, with two forevers instead of three, and drops the comma from lovers cling to each other, and children cling to us. If Wikiquote were right the line would be minted wording and out. So I went past the blogs to a scholarly reproduction of Baldwin's whole text, the Nothing Personal reprint hosted on UMass ScholarWorks, downloaded it and read the last pages. It has three forevers. The sentence is verbatim: For nothing is fixed, forever and forever and forever, it is not fixed; the earth is always shifting, the light is always changing, the sea does not cease to grind down rock. Wikiquote is the corrupt rendering, and it was worth catching, because the triple forever is not ornament: Baldwin plants it on the first page as the advertisers' promise, prevented for twenty-four hours of every day, forever and forever and forever, and the ending takes the phrase back. Cutting one forever would break that. Attribution is not in question and the line is on no misattribution trap. It is Baldwin's own prose, not a character's, so no speaker is owed. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, James Baldwin at 0 of 3, not banned. The quoted sentence opens the penultimate paragraph; the closing lines proper are the ones after it, The sea rises, the light fails, lovers cling to each other, and children cling to us, and so on to the sea engulfs us and the light goes out.
